origin.summary: Leyra grew up in Greyfen watching adults trust boundary maps they could not read. At eighteen she is a junior ward-map apprentice at Vellum Hall, close to earning the right to seal independent surveys.

origin_facts.fact: Leyra grew up in Greyfen beside the eastern ward-line.
Leyra is a formally registered junior boundary cartographer apprenticed to Master Ilyan.
At sixteen Leyra caught a copied boundary label that would have sent a shepherding route into a warded bog.

formative_events.summary: Leyra proved a copied route label was wrong before the map was sealed.
formative_events.impact: She learned that small cartographic errors can become real danger once institutions trust them.

formative_events.summary: Master Ilyan allowed Leyra to assist with a routine wardstone survey.
formative_events.impact: She became fascinated by places where map lines and physical boundaries disagree.

origin_relationships.subject: Master Ilyan
origin_relationships.historical_role: trained Leyra to separate witnessed fact from attractive theory
origin_relationships.unresolved_tension: Leyra has noticed that Ilyan becomes unusually terse whenever Ashen Gate appears in archive work.

origin_relationships.subject: Greyfen ward-keepers
origin_relationships.historical_role: people Leyra grew up around and still feels responsible toward
origin_relationships.unresolved_tension: They trust Leyra personally more than they trust the guild.

unresolved_origin_questions.question: Why does Master Ilyan avoid discussing his earlier surveys near Ashen Gate?

present_situation.summary: Leyra works from Vellum Hall as a junior boundary cartographer, performing supervised re-surveys while preparing for her independent map-seal examination.
present_situation.current_role: junior boundary cartographer under independent map-seal review
present_situation.current_location_context: based at Vellum Hall with authorized field access to Greyfen and the exterior survey markers around Ashen Gate
current_relationship_context: Master Ilyan evaluates her field judgment
Greyfen ward-keepers treat her as one of their own
current_resources: legal copies of the eastern boundary maps
a ward-compass that reacts to witnessed boundary lines
access to ordinary Vellum Hall records
current_pressures: the independent map-seal examination is approaching
spring traffic through Greyfen is increasing
the guild punishes unlicensed crossing of sealed boundaries
current_open_questions: Why is Ashen Gate still legally sealed?
Why does Master Ilyan avoid old Ashen Gate records?
immediate_desires: prove that wonder and discipline can coexist in serious cartography
immediate_avoidances: inventing certainty because a discovery feels important
being dismissed as a reckless village-born apprentice

identity_anchors.statement: Leyra believes a map should never claim more than its maker can honestly witness.
Leyra is drawn to impossible places but refuses to call mystery proof.

core_drives.drive: Earn the right to chart places current maps cannot explain.
Keep border communities from paying the price for elegant but wrong maps.

core_fears.fear: A confident mistake of hers could be sealed into a map other people trust.
Someone she trusts may have hidden important evidence for reasons she cannot yet judge.

internal_tensions.side_b: powerful desire to cross into the unknown
internal_tensions.description: Leyra's best discoveries tempt her to move faster than the rules that make those discoveries trustworthy.

long_term_questions.question: Why do some roads erased from legal maps appear to return?
What did Master Ilyan actually learn at Ashen Gate years ago?

themes: who gets to define a border

main_saga.title: The Unwritten Border
main_saga.goal: Discover why Ashen Gate and other retired boundary lines can begin answering to roads that legal maps say no longer exist.
main_saga.stakes: Wrongly restoring a dangerous road could expose border communities to unstable magic, while wrongly suppressing a real route could leave the guild blind to a changing world.
main_saga.central_mystery: The old boundary network is changing state according to rules the current guild only partly understands.

anchors.title: The Returning Pass
anchors.purpose: Establish credible evidence that Ashen Gate is no longer behaving like a fully sealed boundary.
anchors.target_state: Leyra has a bounded, reusable record that the gate now answers to a path current legal maps do not contain.

anchors.title: The Retired Maps
anchors.purpose: Investigate legal and retired chart history without assuming suppression or conspiracy.
anchors.target_state: Leyra can distinguish missing, retired and deliberately restricted Ashen Gate records.

anchors.title: The People Beside the Line
anchors.purpose: Compare lived border knowledge with guild evidence without treating folklore as proof.
anchors.target_state: Leyra has corroborated which changes around Greyfen are witnessed facts and which remain stories.

anchors.title: The Unwritten Side
anchors.purpose: Earn a lawful opportunity to investigate the reappearing route without predefining what lies beyond it.
anchors.target_state: Leyra gains bounded access or evidence from the far side while preserving uncertainty about the Nameless Vale.

anchors.title: What the Border Is For
anchors.purpose: Bring enough verified evidence together that the true function of the old boundary must be confronted.
anchors.target_state: Leyra and the world possess enough verified evidence to choose how the boundary should be treated without the saga pre-writing that choice.

milestones.summary: Leyra documents a repeatable visible or magical response showing that Ashen Gate currently answers to a path the legal map marks as sealed.
milestones.state_condition: A dated field record establishes one bounded anomaly at Ashen Gate, without proving why the gate changed.
consequence_options: The guild must decide whether a formal re-survey is warranted.
Greyfen gains a concrete reason to watch the old boundary.

milestones.summary: A second survey condition confirms the gate response is not a single accidental compass twitch.
milestones.state_condition: Leyra has corroborating field evidence that the boundary response is real, while cause remains unresolved.
consequence_options: Master Ilyan can no longer dismiss the event as one bad reading.

milestones.summary: Leyra notices an old private field mark associated with Master Ilyan near the exterior survey stones.
milestones.state_condition: The mark establishes only that Ilyan surveyed or marked this site before; it does not establish why or what he knew.
consequence_options: Leyra's trust question becomes more immediate.

milestones.summary: Leyra finds a retired chart showing that Ashen Gate once connected to a named route later removed from legal maps.
milestones.state_condition: A historical route existed, but its removal reason is not yet established.
consequence_options: Archive work becomes relevant to the live anomaly.

milestones.summary: Leyra identifies exactly which years or survey packets are missing or restricted.
milestones.state_condition: The archive gap is bounded without being labeled a cover-up.
consequence_options: Specific records can be requested or sought elsewhere.

milestones.summary: A surviving index links Master Ilyan to an older Ashen Gate survey.
milestones.state_condition: Ilyan's prior involvement becomes documented, while motive and conclusions remain unresolved.
consequence_options: Leyra can ask a precise question instead of making an accusation.

milestones.summary: A Greyfen ward-keeper gives Leyra a first-hand account of a recent boundary oddity.
milestones.state_condition: The account becomes a documented witness statement, not proof of magical cause.
consequence_options: The keeper may become a reusable witness.

milestones.summary: Leyra compares local stories of a returning road against dated physical observations.
milestones.state_condition: Folklore is separated into corroborated details and unsupported embellishment.
consequence_options: Some old place-names become useful search terms.

milestones.summary: Two independent local observations agree on one recent environmental or ward-line change.
milestones.state_condition: A local change is corroborated without proving it caused the gate to reopen.
consequence_options: A formal field revisit becomes easier to justify.

milestones.summary: Leyra earns lawful permission for a bounded crossing or equivalent remote survey beyond Ashen Gate.
milestones.state_condition: Future investigation can proceed without turning reckless trespass into the required solution.
consequence_options: The guild recognizes the anomaly as survey-worthy.

milestones.summary: Leyra obtains a second independent boundary anchor associated with the returning route.
milestones.state_condition: The route exists as more than a single-gate artifact, but destination and purpose remain unresolved.
consequence_options: The Nameless Vale becomes a legitimate survey question.

milestones.summary: Leyra establishes where her evidence stops at the edge of the Nameless Vale.
milestones.state_condition: The far-side unknown remains unknown rather than being filled with invented lore.
consequence_options: The next investigation has a safe epistemic boundary.

milestones.summary: Multiple verified sources establish the rule that governs why the old boundary can change state.
milestones.state_condition: The mechanism is confirmed at the level required for public map policy.
consequence_options: The guild must reconsider how sealed roads are monitored.

milestones.summary: Evidence establishes what Master Ilyan actually knew and what he did not know during his earlier Ashen Gate survey.
milestones.state_condition: Leyra can judge Ilyan's past action with context rather than suspicion alone.
consequence_options: Their relationship may deepen, fracture or change on earned grounds.

milestones.summary: The verified evidence leaves more than one defensible way to respond to the returning route.
milestones.state_condition: The world has explicit response options without the saga precommitting Leyra's final choice.
consequence_options: A future choice can affect maps, access and Greyfen.

hidden_truths.question: What rule allows a legally sealed road to begin answering again?
hidden_truths.hidden_statement: Ashen Gate is one node in an older oath-road network whose wardstones can reactivate when three surviving boundary anchors fall back into geometric agreement after long landscape shifts.

hidden_truths.question: What did Master Ilyan learn at Ashen Gate years ago?
hidden_truths.hidden_statement: Ilyan observed one anomalous gate response but failed to reproduce it from a second anchor, so he left a private field mark and withheld a formal reopening claim; why he never disclosed even that failed test remains unresolved.

hidden_truths.question: What is the Nameless Vale, and why was it removed from legal maps?

reveal_steps.summary: Sufficient independent anchors establish the rule governing road reactivation.
Records and testimony establish the limits of Ilyan's earlier evidence.

any_of.condition: Ilyan voluntarily explains his earlier survey

latent_side_sagas.premise: Greyfen's trust in guild maps may change as Leyra's discoveries affect decisions near the ward-line.
latent_side_sagas.why_it_matters: Keeps institutional consequences grounded in people Leyra knows.

latent_side_sagas.premise: Leyra and Master Ilyan may have to renegotiate what professional trust means when incomplete old evidence surfaces.
latent_side_sagas.why_it_matters: Gives the mystery a personal relationship dimension without pre-deciding betrayal.

any_of.condition: any partial or confirmed evidence surfaces

creation_constraints: Magic must follow rule-bound cartographic and boundary logic.
New durable facts must not explain why Ashen Gate reopened before the relevant reveal becomes eligible.
New NPCs should have plausible links to guild or border life.
forbidden_creations: Arbitrary spellcasting that bypasses surveying and evidence
Early confirmation of the Nameless Vale's purpose
Predetermined proof that Master Ilyan acted maliciously

integration_rules: Reuse established named locations in the fixture before inventing durable new ones.
Keep legal maps, witnessed surveys and ward responses distinct forms of authority.
